headline: GOLD STALLS AT $4,533 AS TRUMP HEADS TO US-IRAN MEETING; Metals Markets Await a 'Deal'
snippet: Gold trades at $4,533/oz Monday with no US-Iran deal agreed yet, though hopes remain high and Trump is reportedly attending a decisive meeting today. A peace agreement could dent safe-haven demand; prolonged conflict keeps a floor under prices and supports the broader precious metals complex.

headline: BULL MARKET INTACT: Gold Up 119% Since Jan. 2024 — Why the Trend Is Still Your Friend
snippet: Kai Hoffmann tells Money Metals host Mike Maharrey why gold's structural bull market is intact despite the ~20% correction from 2026 highs near $5,600, citing relentless central bank accumulation, accelerating de-dollarization, and US fiscal deterioration as the supports that haven't changed — and likely won't.

headline: GOLD'S BIGGEST CORRECTION IN YEARS — How High-Net-Worth Investors Are Responding
snippet: With gold down ~20% from its 2026 peak near $5,600, wealth managers surveyed by CEOWORLD report that high-net-worth clients are treating the pullback as a structural entry point — adding physical, royalty companies, and selective junior miners rather than reducing exposure.

headline: FALLING WEDGE BREAKOUT: Gold Reclaims $4,500 — Technical Traders Eye $4,657 Next
snippet: Gold broke out of a multi-week falling wedge pattern and reclaimed the critical $4,500 level. Analysts are watching $4,550–$4,600 as the next resistance cluster, with the first upside target at $4,657 and a secondary target near $4,891 if momentum accelerates — key levels for junior miners whose share prices track spot closely.

headline: ALASKA LEADS: State Ends Sales Taxes on Gold and Silver, Enacts Legal Tender Law
snippet: Alaska enacted legislation on May 29 removing all municipal sales taxes on gold and silver specie and declaring the metals legal tender under state law — the strongest state-level affirmation of monetary metals status in recent US history, and a potential legislative template for other states.

headline: GOLD ETF INFLOWS FLIP POSITIVE for First Time Since April — Institutions Return to Metals
snippet: U.S. Global Investors' weekly Gold SWOT analysis flags that net gold ETF inflows turned positive for the first time since early April, with North American funds accounting for $824 million of the demand recovery. Institutional re-engagement at current levels is a significant shift from the seven-week outflow streak.

headline: COPPER HOLDS $6.40/LB — AI Data Center Demand + Chilean Smelter Cuts Power Second Monthly Gain
snippet: Copper futures held near $6.40/lb heading into June, on track for a second consecutive monthly gain. AI infrastructure electrification demand and Chilean smelter curtailments are tightening physical availability, while a US Commerce Department report due June 30 could recommend further tariffs on refined copper imports — adding policy risk to an already tight market.

headline: CAMECO CLEARS FLOOD DISRUPTION: McArthur River + Key Lake Return to Full Uranium Output
snippet: Cameco confirmed full production has resumed at McArthur River mine and Key Lake mill after May flooding in northern Saskatchewan partially collapsed the primary supply bridge, cutting off critical materials to the world's largest high-grade uranium operation. Full-year guidance of 19.5–21.5 million lbs U3O8 (Cameco share) is unchanged.

headline: 50,000 METERS MOBILIZED: Goliath Resources Kicks Off Biggest-Ever Surebet Drill in B.C.'s Golden Triangle
snippet: Goliath Resources (TSX-V: GOT) has mobilized rigs for a fully funded 50,000-metre expansion program at its Surebet discovery in B.C.'s Golden Triangle, targeting both lateral and depth extensions across 46 gold-rich stacked lodes. With 156,000 metres drilled and all zones still open, this is among the most active high-grade gold exploration campaigns on the TSXV.

headline: LITHIUM CLIMBS AGAIN in 2026 — Battery Storage Set to Hit 31% of LCE Demand as Oversupply Era Ends
snippet: Spot battery-grade lithium carbonate has surged ~95% from its June 2025 low to ~$24,000/tonne, powered by energy storage deployment that analysts project will consume 31% of global LCE by year-end — up from 23% in 2025. The structural surplus that crushed the sector through 2024–25 is narrowing faster than most forecasters expected.
